P01.note: Needs the censure sentence plus 'record the members' own votes, each in the member's hand' and 'no member was ever censured'; distractors are not near-misses.

P02.note: Self-declared emergency plus 31 of 40 summers points to loophole; 'lever' is a real near-miss for a tool the upstream state used.

P03.note: 'taking the evening train home' rules out dormitory; granary and garrison have no support.

P04.note: 'Few members read past its first pages' kills gospel and handbook; the proceeds sentence gives fundraiser.

P05.note: Debts/cursing/tavern softened to dressmaker/'sir'/tea shop; 'printed' kills shelved and the unchanged 1880s setting kills updated.

P06.note: Decade-long stall then vote in three months gives jolted; 'before the legislature for a decade' kills launched, but 'jolted' is a slightly loose fit for supplying decisive figures.

P07.note: Freak-event judgment on past record plus minimal repair gives complacent; bureaucratic is a plausible near-miss.

P08.note: 'in short, plain sentences, and he never remarks on any of them' gives deadpan and kills florid and didactic.

P09.note: Fixed seats, weekly reading, and diaries recording the reading rather than content together give ritual; distractors are weak.

P10.note: 'No agreement appears in either town's minutes or letters' gives tacit almost alone; 'almost no cut weirs' kills token and both towns acting kills unilateral.

P11.note: 'Her reviews weighed each play's strengths against its faults' gives judicious and kills mercurial and insistent.

P12.note: 'dressed as ordinary customers ... and left without a word' gives furtive directly.

P13.note: 'printed the valley's revised plan as its standard drawing, from which the terraces of nine other districts were then built' is the definition of prototype.

P14.note: Fish carriers turned into furnishings gives repurposed; 'weaving more baskets than ever' makes rekindled a near-miss, though the craft never lapsed.

P15.note: 'bare concrete ... plain rows of bulbs ... struck every carving, mural, and carpet' gives austere; 'low reading rooms' kills airy.

P16.note: 'fined ... a few shillings, far below what the law allowed, and let those who admitted the offense keep their goods' gives lenient.

P17.note: Forty dormant years, one barge, office closed, local dealers resume: awakened; 'closed its office the next spring' kills cornered.

P18.note: Two printed songs sung as one twenty-verse song gives merged; mangled is a pejorative near-miss.

P19.note: Apprentices trained, released, then nine of eleven yards run by village men combine to give incubator.

P20.note: 'X-ray machine, its operating tables, and most of its surgeons were moved to the city one by one, as the new building needed them' gives cannibalized alone.

P21.note: 'The river behind the jam rose into a lake' states the damming outright.

P22.note: 'set the idea aside' plus 'again presented the ridge as the springs' source' gives rehabilitated; 'The 1931 survey' is introduced with a definite article as if already known.

P23.note: 'From the island's single hill a lookout could see forty miles of the strait' gives watchtower; 'thin soil and almost no trade' kills storehouse and tollgate.

P24.note: Home county filling half the sheet plus sales in that county's towns, against proportional rivals, gives provincial.

P25.note: Features taught as 'errors' all removed gives cleansed; 'keeps its full length and its speed' kills clipped.

P26.note: Lessons plus promotions to weighmen, clerks, foremen and sons to university give ladder; the mine-records sentence nearly decides it alone.

P27.note: 'the candidates took turns on that balcony on successive market mornings' makes platform both literal and figurative.

P28.note: Unexplained acts plus 'offers no motive for any of these acts' give puzzle; pivot is defensible since the locket thread runs through him.

P29.note: 'showed the forest floor through bare crowns' gives defoliated; new leaves each spring kill felled.

P30.note: 'opened both roles to anyone who had worked that year's harvest' gives democratized directly.

P31.note: Soft orchestra, smooth tenor, 'easier on the ear' give sweetened; 'arranged two more hill ballads the same way' makes standardized a near-miss.

P32.note: Village clubs disband and survivors are in mill or market towns gives urbanized; tamed and unbalanced are plausible near-misses.

P33.note: 'The letters ... held what her diaries and her other letters leave out' plus 'He told no one' is the definition of confidant.

P34.note: Fines exceed the crews' cost ('a fraction of what it collected') gives profitable; 'less than half of what a laborer earned' kills onerous; porous is a near-miss.

P35.note: Messages left, sorted by village, and carried out give switchboard; needs the routing sentences together.

P36.note: Land, western-elected abbots, and bishop's support kept the eastern lord short: counterweight; checkpoint is a location-based lure.

P37.note: Overflow over a bank and passed to the bay within a day gives spillway; sponge is the near-miss, killed only by 'within a day' and the creeks emptying into the bay.

P38.note: Lone no vote each year under a unanimity rule gives holdout; gatekeeper is defensible since her vote blocked the merger.

P39.note: 'published, almost unchanged, as a book of essays' gives literary; 'few counts' kills methodical.

P40.note: 'copied every notebook out afresh with figures that matched his papers and emptied the remaining samples down the drain' gives accomplice alone.
